name: Bike
cue: Pedal smooth circles and keep your hips still on the saddle.
research: research.json biomech.bike: upright bike, trunk 20 deg forward, sit bones on the saddle (ischia pin), bottom bracket 0.14 H in front of and 0.433 H below the hip joint (hip-to-BB line 72 deg from horizontal, research 70-73), 170 mm (0.0955 H) cranks, pedal spindles 0.08 H out from the midline with the crank arms inboard at 0.03 H so the ankles clear them. Saddle height set for ~32 deg of knee flexion at the bottom of the stroke (research 25-35, never > 40): knee 32 -> 115 (min at 160, max at 340 deg of crank; research ~30 at 160-170 and ~112 at 340-350), hip flexion 44 -> 97 (research 48 -> 97 against the trunk). Ankle keyed by crank angle: -4 in the power phase, -16 in the early upstroke. Handlebar grips 0.071 H (13 cm) above the sit bones and 0.369 H (66 cm) ahead of the saddle's front edge; the reach is set by the researched arm angles (shoulder flexion ~56, elbows 20) with the trunk at 20 deg. The saddle is 18 cm wide and 14 cm long with no nose (this rig's inner thighs meet at the midline, so a nose would cut into them); measured from where a standard saddle's nose would sit, about 17 cm ahead of the sit bones, the reach is 52 cm (research 45-55). The seat post rises from the base beam to under the saddle at 71 deg (research 70-73). A dark drive housing encloses the bottom bracket, the belt and the flywheel (a teardrop in the crank plane, 0.04 H thick, mounted on the seat post and the front post); the crank arms turn just outside it. Constant cadence 80 rpm (0.75 s per revolution). Primary: vastus lateralis, vastus medialis and gluteus maximus (the research primaries; rectus femoris is a research secondary and is not drawn, so the thigh glow is the lateral vastus band rather than the whole thigh); secondary: calves. Muscle timing (crank angle of peak activation, left leg; the right leg runs 180 deg behind): vasti 40, gluteus maximus 75, soleus 110, gastrocnemius 160. motion.offset 180 puts the near (right) leg in its power phase at the verification peak frame. Geometry: tools/design/bike.mjs. Secondary: none drawn (one idea: quads and glutes drive the pedal). The calves as amber secondary covered the whole shank as a tan tint rather than light.

targets.note: Cycle mode: the start and peak frames are 90 deg of crank apart, so the leg angles cannot be A/B targets. They are checked as loop extremes (R: [[min band], [max band]]): knee 25-35 at bottom dead centre (the brief's saddle-height rule, knee <= 40) and 105-118 at the top, hip 38-58 / 87-107, ankle -20..-12 / -6..0 (tools/design/bike.mjs). The trunk and arms are constant and checked by A/B.
